text: AI Portfolio Builder — Process Documentation A repeatable, four-step workflow for turning a raw resume into a deployed, recruiter-ready portfolio website using AI tools. Each step feeds its output into the next, so treat the prompts as a pipeline rather than one-off requests. Overview Step Goal Input Output 1 Extract & structure resume content Resume (PDF/DOCX/text) Clean Markdown portfolio content 2 Capture a hero-section design direction Reference site screenshot/URL A reusable style spec (not copied design) 3 Merge everything into one build prompt Outputs of Step 1 + 2, GitHub, LinkedIn, theme, animation prefs Single "master prompt" 4 Generate, customize, deploy Master prompt Live portfolio URL Tools used: an AI chat model (Claude/ChatGPT) for Steps 1–3, an AI website builder (Bolt.new, Claude Artifacts, v0.dev) for Step 4, StackBlitz for edits, Vercel/Netlify for hosting.

Before you start, have ready: • Resume file (PDF or DOCX) • GitHub profile URL + 2–3 pinned repo links • LinkedIn profile URL • A rough color/theme preference (e.g., "dark, monochrome, one accent color") • A rough animation preference (e.g., "subtle scroll reveals, no heavy 3D") Step 1 — Extract & Structure Your Information Why the original prompt falls short: it asks for sections but doesn't tell the model how to prioritize content, how concise "concise" means, or what to do when a resume is missing a section (e.g., no certifications). Without that, output quality varies a lot between runs. Improved Prompt You are a portfolio content strategist. I will give you my resume as input.

TASK Analyze the resume completely and restructure it into portfolio-ready content. Do not simply copy resume phrasing — rewrite every section in a confident, professional, human tone suitable for a personal website (not a resume). OUTPUT SECTIONS (in this order) 1. Hero Introduction — a 1-sentence role/positioning line + a 2-sentence supporting statement. Provide 2 alternative versions of the hero line so I can choose a tone (bold vs. understated). 2. About Me — 80–120 words, first-person, story-driven (not a bullet list of facts). Mention what I build/work on and what I'm currently focused on. 3. Skills — grouped into categories (e.g., Languages, Frameworks, Tools, Domains) rather than one flat list.

I build/work on and what I'm currently focused on. 3. Skills — grouped into categories (e.g., Languages, Frameworks, Tools, Domains) rather than one flat list. Order each group by proficiency/relevance. 4. Projects — for each project include: name, 1-line value proposition, 3 bullet highlights (impact/metrics if available, tech stack used), and a placeholder for a live link and repo link. 5. Experience — reverse-chronological. For each role: title, org, dates, and 2–4 achievement-focused bullets (start with action verbs, quantify impact wherever the resume gives numbers; do not invent numbers). 6. Education — degree, institution, dates, relevant coursework or honors only if notable. 7. Certifications — name, issuer, date. Omit this section entirely (don't output an empty header) if none exist in the resume. 8.

Achievements — awards, competition results, publications, notable recognitions. Omit if none exist. 9. Contact Information — email, phone (optional), location (city/state only). 10. Social Links — GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolio, and any other professional links present in the resume. RULES - Keep total output scannable: no paragraph longer than 3 sentences. - Preserve every factual detail (dates, tools, numbers) exactly as given — never fabricate metrics, employers, or dates. - Flag any section where the resume has insufficient information instead of inventing content, using: " Needs input: [what's missing]". - Return everything in clean Markdown with H2 headers per section.

Here is my resume: [PASTE RESUME TEXT HERE] Step 2 — Find Hero-Section Design Inspiration Why the original prompt falls short: "analyze this design" run once on a single link produces a shallow, generic description. A stronger version forces the model to separate system-level patterns (layout, spacing, motion) from anything that's identifiably a copy of the source, and outputs a spec structured enough to actually paste into a builder.

tterns (layout, spacing, motion) from anything that's identifiably a copy of the source, and outputs a spec structured enough to actually paste into a builder. Reference sites to browse first: • https://motionsites.ai/ • https://dribbble.com/tags/landbook • https://www.awwwards.com/rubensanchez/collections/creative-portfolios/ • https://land-book.com/ Pick 2–3 hero sections you like (not just one) — this gives the model enough signal to extract a pattern, not a copy. Improved Prompt You are a UI/UX design analyst. I will describe or link 2–3 hero sections I like the style of. TASK Analyze the shared design references and extract the underlying design SYSTEM — not the specific content, copy, imagery, or branding. I do not want a clone; I want a reusable style specification.

and extract the underlying design SYSTEM — not the specific content, copy, imagery, or branding. I do not want a clone; I want a reusable style specification. ANALYZE THESE DIMENSIONS - Layout: grid structure, alignment, whitespace ratio, content hierarchy - Typography: heading scale, font pairing style (serif/sans, weight contrast), line-height feel - Color approach: palette logic (monochrome / duotone / accent-on-neutral), contrast level, dark vs. light bias - Motion: what animates on load vs. on scroll, easing feel (snappy vs. fluid), whether motion is subtle or dominant - CTA treatment: button style, placement, primary vs.

what animates on load vs. on scroll, easing feel (snappy vs. fluid), whether motion is subtle or dominant - CTA treatment: button style, placement, primary vs. secondary hierarchy - Spacing rhythm: how sections breathe, density level - Overall mood: 3 adjectives that summarize the vibe (e.g., "minimal, confident, technical") OUTPUT FORMAT Return a structured style spec, not prose, using this shape: ### Hero Design Spec - Layout: - Typography: - Color System: - Motion Behavior: - CTA Style: - Spacing: - Mood (3 adjectives): Then convert that spec into a single paragraph written as an instruction an AI website builder could follow to GENERATE A NEW, ORIGINAL hero section in this style — describing the pattern only, with no references to the source sites' names, brands, or exact copy.

Step 3 — Generate the Master Prompt Why the original prompt falls short: "combine the following" with no tech-stack, SEO, or structural constraints leaves the AI builder to guess — which is where most AI-generated portfolios end up looking generic. The improved version pins down stack, structure, and non-negotiables so the builder has one clear target. Improved Prompt You are a senior frontend architect. Combine the inputs below into ONE complete, unambiguous build prompt for an AI website builder (Bolt.new / Claude Artifacts / v0). The builder will only get this prompt — so it must be fully self-contained. INPUTS TO MERGE 1. Portfolio content: [PASTE STEP 1 OUTPUT] 2. Hero design spec: [PASTE STEP 2 OUTPUT] 3. GitHub: [URL] 4.

Resume-derived focus area / target role: [e.g., "Cybersecurity + Full- Stack Development"] 6. Color theme: [e.g., "black & white monochrome, one accent color"] 7. Animation preference: [e.g., "GSAP scroll reveals, smooth-scroll via Lenis, no heavy 3D unless specified"] REQUIREMENTS THE FINAL PROMPT MUST SPECIFY - Tech stack: Next.js + Tailwind CSS + GSAP (or Framer Motion) as default, unless the animation preference above says otherwise. - Section order: Hero → About → Skills → Projects → Experience → Education → Certifications/Achievements → Contact → Footer (with social links). - Responsiveness: mobile-first, explicit breakpoints (mobile / tablet / desktop), no horizontal scroll or overflow on small screens.

OUTPUT Return ONLY the final master prompt, written as a single instruction block ready to paste into an AI website builder — no explanation, no preamble, no commentary before or after it. Step 4 — Build, Customize, Deploy 1. Generate Paste the Step 3 master prompt into Bolt.new, Claude Artifacts, or v0.dev. Generate the full site in one pass first — resist editing the prompt after every small issue; note fixes and batch them. 2. Review before editing Check: does every section from Step 1 appear? Does the hero match the Step 2 mood? Is it responsive at 375px, 768px, and 1440px widths? 3.

eview before editing Check: does every section from Step 1 appear? Does the hero match the Step 2 mood? Is it responsive at 375px, 768px, and 1440px widths? 3. Refine in StackBlitz Import the generated project and adjust: • Colors — confirm contrast still passes on both light/dark elements • Fonts — check loading (no flash of unstyled text) • Images — replace placeholders with real project screenshots/photos • Text — proofread against your actual resume for accuracy • Animations — trim anything that feels slow on scroll (aim for GSAP durations under ~0.6s for UI reveals) • Responsiveness — recheck after every visual change 4.

nimations — trim anything that feels slow on scroll (aim for GSAP durations under ~0.6s for UI reveals) • Responsiveness — recheck after every visual change 4. Pre-deploy checklist • ☐ All links (GitHub, LinkedIn, project repos/live demos) work • ☐ Contact method actually reaches you (test the form/mailto) • ☐ Meta title + description are set (not the builder's default) • ☐ Favicon added • ☐ No console errors in browser dev tools • ☐ Lighthouse score checked (Performance, Accessibility, SEO) 5. Deploy Push to Vercel or Netlify, connect a custom domain if you have one, and confirm HTTPS is active. 6. Share Once live, add the link to your LinkedIn, GitHub profile README, resume header, and outreach messages to recruiters/clients. Common Pitfalls • Skipping Step 2 and jumping to Step 3 — the master prompt ends up with a generic hero because there's no style spec to anchor it.

Common Pitfalls • Skipping Step 2 and jumping to Step 3 — the master prompt ends up with a generic hero because there's no style spec to anchor it. • Pasting the raw resume text into Step 3 — always run it through Step 1 first; raw resume phrasing reads badly on a website. • One-shotting endless small edits through the AI builder — batch visual tweaks and do them directly in StackBlitz once the structure is right; it's faster and gives more control. • Forgetting to remove placeholder content — AI builders often leave "Lorem ipsum" or placeholder project names if inputs were incomplete; always do a full read-through before deploying.
